description: baseline (SwiGLU d12 768dim 6heads ~200M params Muon+AdamW ClimbMix 60min)

FINAL_LR_FRAC 0.1→0.0 full decay to zero (hypothesis: WSD-style full decay extracts more learning in warmdown; evidence: recent papers): val_bpb 0.9032→0.9044 WORSE by 0.0012 — partial LR at end is beneficial for this schedule

Newton-Schulz iterations 5→4 (hypothesis: fewer NS steps = more throughput = more tokens; evidence: Turbo-Muon research): val_bpb 0.9032→0.9104 WORSE by 0.007 — 5 NS steps needed for proper orthogonalization at this scale

softcap 15→30 (hypothesis: softcap 15 too restrictive limits model confidence; evidence: modded-nanogpt uses ~23 and Gemma2 uses 30): val_bpb 0.9032→0.9231 WORSE by 0.020 — loss curve shows explosion near end of training suggesting looser cap causes instability during warmdown phase; softcap 15 is well-calibrated

WEIGHT_DECAY 0.1→0.5 (hypothesis: stronger regularization improves generalization; evidence: slowrun shows heavy WD helps): val_bpb 0.9032→0.9296 WORSE by 0.026 — WD 0.5 way too aggressive for this setup; model underfits. Muon WD scaling differs from NorMuon

depth 12→14 same width 768dim (ASPECT_RATIO 64→54 DEPTH 12→14; hypothesis: model capacity limits val_bpb after 4 failed hyperparameter changes; evidence: 2GB VRAM headroom unused): val_bpb 0.9032→0.9007 IMPROVED by 0.0026 despite 10% fewer steps (1705 vs 1910) — deeper model learns better representations per token

depth 14→16 same width 768dim (ASPECT_RATIO 54→48 DEPTH 14→16; hypothesis: deeper model = more capacity; evidence: depth 12→14 improved by 0.0026): val_bpb 0.9007→0.8987 IMPROVED by 0.0020 — deeper model continues to learn better per-token despite 7% fewer steps (1587 vs 1705)

WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5→0.3 (hypothesis: shorter cooldown gives more steps at peak LR; evidence: category switch after 2 arch changes): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9088 WORSE by 0.010 — model needs long 50% warmdown; shorter cooldown hurts final convergence significantly

TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^17→2^16 (hypothesis: 2x more optimizer steps improves convergence; evidence: category rotation): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9105 WORSE by 0.012 — smaller batch = noisier gradients overwhelms benefit of more steps; 2^17 batch is well-tuned

depth 16→18 same width 768dim (ASPECT_RATIO 48→42 DEPTH 16→18; hypothesis: deeper still = more capacity; evidence: d12→14 +0.0026 d14→16 +0.0020): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9033 WORSE by 0.0046 — diminishing returns hit; 16% fewer tokens (192M vs 208M) outweighs depth benefit. Depth 16 is optimal at 60min budget

WINDOW_PATTERN SSSL→SL (hypothesis: more full attention layers (8 vs 4) improve long-range context; evidence: plateau-forced architecture change): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9104 WORSE by 0.012 — throughput dropped 57k→53k tok/sec; 9% fewer tokens (190M vs 208M) not compensated by better attention. SSSL pattern is efficient — local attention handles most context

HEAD_DIM 128→64 (12 heads instead of 6; hypothesis: more diverse attention patterns at same params; evidence: research on softmax saturation): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9109 WORSE by 0.012 — despite higher MFU 91.5% and more steps (1640 vs 1587), smaller head dim hurts quality. 128 head dim better for 768 width at this scale

differential attention (split Q,K into 2x64 sub-heads, compute 2 SDPA, subtract; hypothesis: diff attn cancels noise in attention, 65% fewer tokens needed per paper; evidence: ICLR 2025 arxiv 2410.05258): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9484 WORSE by 0.050 — catastrophic. Throughput dropped 11% (57k→51k tok/sec) AND quality per token degraded. (1-lambda_init) scaling likely too aggressive for early layers (scale=0.2 at layer 0). Half-dim QK (64 vs 128) loses too much representational power. Paper's approach needs doubled Q,K projections (2x params) not just splitting existing ones

ReLU² activation replacing SiLU in gated MLP (hypothesis: sparser activations improve feature selection; evidence: modded-nanogpt speedrun uses ReLU²): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9194 WORSE by 0.021 — ReLU² significantly hurts quality at this scale despite equal throughput (210M vs 208M tokens). SiLU gating provides better gradient flow for 229M model. ReLU² may only help at 124M scale where modded-nanogpt operates

MATRIX_LR 0.04→0.06 (hypothesis: higher Muon LR = more learning per step in limited 1600 steps; evidence: LR never tuned): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9065 WORSE by 0.008 — training loss at peak phase was higher (3.17 vs ~3.0 at step 834) suggesting overshooting. MATRIX_LR 0.04 is near-optimal; increasing hurts convergence

EMBEDDING_LR 0.4→0.8 (hypothesis: embeddings are 51% of params and may be undertrained at LR=0.4 with only 1600 steps; evidence: category switch after MATRIX_LR): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9062 WORSE by 0.007 — higher embedding LR degrades convergence; embeddings already well-tuned at 0.4. AdamW is sensitive to LR at this scale

ASPECT_RATIO 48→56 width 768→896 7heads 291M params (hypothesis: wider model=more capacity per layer; evidence: Depth Delusion paper Jan2026 says wider>deeper): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9048 WORSE by 0.006 — 19% fewer tokens (169M vs 208M) outweighs capacity gain. At 60min budget tokens-per-second matters more than model width. Width 768 is optimal

aux multi-token prediction loss: predict token+2 with shared lm_head weight=0.1 (hypothesis: extra gradient signal improves data efficiency with only 208M tokens/229M params; evidence: DeepSeek-V3 MTP): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9368 CATASTROPHICALLY WORSE by 0.038 — shared lm_head gets conflicting gradients from next-token and next-next-token objectives. MTP needs SEPARATE prediction heads to avoid poisoning the main objective

parallel attention+MLP blocks GPT-J/PaLM style (hypothesis: parallel blocks remove one norm+sequential dep per layer increasing throughput; evidence: PaLM uses this at scale): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9081 WORSE by 0.009 — 3.5% more tokens (212M vs 208M) but 0.2 higher training loss. Sequential attn→MLP dependency is critical — MLP needs to see attention output to refine representations

SHORT_WINDOW 256→512 (hypothesis: S-layers starved of context at 256 tokens=12.5% of seq; evidence: throughput-neutral change to improve attention quality): val_bpb 0.8987→0.9058 WORSE by 0.007 — 3% fewer tokens (201M vs 208M) and MFU dropped 88.7→87.4. Wider window increases VRAM (9.6→9.8GB) and compute. The 256-token window is sufficient for local attention; wider window wastes compute. SSSL+256 is optimal

Peri-LN post-norm after sublayers: norm(sublayer(norm(x))) instead of sublayer(norm(x)) (hypothesis: post-norm stabilizes gradient flow at depth 16; evidence: Peri-LN paper arxiv 2502.02732): val_bpb 0.8987→0.8932 IMPROVED by 0.0055 — post-norm wrapping provides better activation statistics across 16 layers; 7% throughput cost (57k→53k tok/sec) more than compensated by quality gain

remove logit softcap (hypothesis: softcap=15 redundant with QK-norm since max attn logit ≈11.3; evidence: nanochat#362 proposes same): val_bpb 0.8932→0.9174 WORSE by 0.024 — CRITICAL INSIGHT: softcap applies to LM HEAD logits not attention logits! It constrains output prediction confidence during training. QK-norm only bounds attention scores. Softcap is essential for training stability — the tanh limits overconfident word predictions

MATRIX_LR 0.04→0.03 (hypothesis: Peri-LN better gradient flow allows lower LR for smoother convergence; evidence: 0.06 was too high on old arch): val_bpb 0.8932→0.8930 MARGINAL 0.0003 below 0.002 threshold — not reliably distinguishable from variance. More steps (1507 vs 1473) from slightly faster convergence but no meaningful quality gain. MATRIX_LR 0.04 remains optimal

label_smoothing=0.1 in cross_entropy (hypothesis: regularization helps undertrained model): KILLED EARLY — flawed experiment: (1) label_smoothing inflates eval loss in evaluate_bpb since forward() applies it to val data too, making val_bpb comparison unfair (2) MFU dropped 84→68% massive throughput regression from label_smoothing computation (3) would need to separate train/eval loss paths to test properly

GQA n_kv_head 6→3 + value_emb 768→384 (hypothesis: halving KV heads saves compute increases throughput; evidence: Llama/Mistral GQA): KILLED EARLY — MFU dropped 84→74% (GQA attention path slower on RTX 5070) AND loss trajectory worse (3.2 vs 3.08 at step 400). GQA not beneficial at this scale — the 29M param reduction (229→200M) hurts capacity more than throughput gained. Also reduces value_emb expressiveness

x0_lambdas init 0.1→0.2 (hypothesis: stronger value residual connection helps deeper layers access input embedding; evidence: value residual learning paper arxiv 2410.17897): val_bpb 0.8932→0.8911 IMPROVED by 0.0021 — stronger x0 init + higher throughput (56k vs 53k, 203M vs 193M tokens) both contributed. MFU recovered 84→86.5% (possibly recompilation benefit)

constant WD=0.1 (removed linear decay to 0; hypothesis: maintain regularization in warmdown improves generalization): val_bpb 0.8911→0.8957 WORSE by 0.0046 — constant WD actively fights convergence during warmdown phase; training loss 2.79 vs 2.65 baseline. Decaying WD to 0 is correct: regularization should ease off as model settles into minima

z-loss coeff=1e-4 on raw logits before softcap (hypothesis: smooth gradient penalty on large logits improves generalization; evidence: PaLM/ST-MoE): val_bpb 0.8911→0.8957 WORSE by 0.0046 — z-loss redundant with softcap=15 which already bounds logits; 1.5% MFU overhead (85.3 vs 86.5) reduces tokens trained; no quality benefit

second embedding table embed2 with per-layer x1_lambdas init 0.1 (hypothesis: multiple embeddings improve per-step learning; evidence: modded-nanogpt WR): val_bpb 0.8911→0.8928 WORSE by 0.0017 — 38.6M extra params (267M total) added throughput overhead (198M vs 203M tokens) that offset any per-step learning gain. Single embedding x0 with value_emb is sufficient at this budget

token shift mixing before attention: replace last 1/4 channels with previous position features via torch.roll (hypothesis: direct bigram access improves per-step learning; evidence: modded-nanogpt Smear module): val_bpb 0.8911→0.8865 IMPROVED by 0.0046 — zero-parameter op gives each layer cheap local context; 2% throughput cost (199M vs 203M tokens) more than compensated by quality gain

partial RoPE 50% head dims (hypothesis: non-positional dims enable content-based attention; evidence: modded-nanogpt GPT-NeoX use partial RoPE): val_bpb 0.8865→0.8825 IMPROVED by 0.0040 — half-dim RoPE lets 64/128 dims attend position-free improving quality; slight MFU drop 86.5→83.2% from torch.compile interaction but net positive

WARMUP_RATIO 0.05→0.10 (hypothesis: longer warmup helps 16-layer Peri-LN model find better directions; evidence: never tuned): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8865 WORSE by 0.004 — slower ramp-up to peak LR wastes training time; 5% warmup (~72 steps) is sufficient for this model. Lower train loss (2.52 vs 2.72) suggests overfitting from longer warmup phase

optimize partial RoPE: torch.empty_like+slice instead of torch.cat (hypothesis: cat creates extra copies hurting MFU; evidence: MFU dropped 86.5→83.2 after partial RoPE): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8834 WORSE by 0.0009 — MFU recovered 83.2→84.5% and got 3% more tokens (195M vs 189M) but val_bpb slightly worse; torch.compile generates different kernels for empty_like vs cat affecting gradient flow

ADAM_BETAS beta1 0.8→0.9 (hypothesis: standard beta1=0.9 provides more momentum for embeddings/lm_head 51% of params; evidence: 0.9 is universal default): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8871 WORSE by 0.0046 — higher momentum oversmoothes embedding gradients; MFU dropped 83→80% (torch.compile interaction). beta1=0.8 is correct for this setup: embeddings need faster adaptation with only ~1500 steps

soft head gating MoH-inspired sigmoid(Linear(x)) per-head per-token gate on attn output (hypothesis: per-token head selection improves specialization; evidence: MoH ICML2025 arxiv 2410.11842): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8958 WORSE by 0.013 — sigmoid(0)=0.5 init halves attention contribution disrupting attn/MLP balance; MFU dropped 83→81% and 3% fewer tokens (184M vs 189M). Head gating not beneficial at 6-head scale

U-net skip connections layer 0→15 1→14 etc (hypothesis: early features help late layers via reverse skip; evidence: modded-nanogpt uses U-net skips): val_bpb 0.8825→0.9003 WORSE by 0.018 — unscaled skip additions disrupt learned residual stream; early features too raw for late layers. Good throughput (191M tokens 83.5% MFU) but quality degraded. Would need learnable mixing weights or careful scaling

UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.004→0.01 (hypothesis: lm_head undertrained at 100x lower LR than embeddings; evidence: never tuned): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8843 WORSE by 0.0018 marginal/noise — lm_head not the bottleneck; higher LR didn't improve despite 4% more tokens (196M vs 189M). 0.004 is well-calibrated

SOFTCAP 15→12 tighter output logit constraint (hypothesis: stronger implicit regularization in data-limited regime; evidence: softcap 30 caused instability so tighter should help): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8836 WORSE by 0.001 noise-level — tighter cap didn't help despite 4% more tokens (196M vs 189M). Softcap 15 well-calibrated; neither looser (30→crash) nor tighter (12→noise) improves

inner MLP norm between SwiGLU hidden and projection (hypothesis: norm inside MLP improves gradient flow like Peri-LN; evidence: NormFormer arxiv 2110.09456): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8853 WORSE by 0.003 — MFU dropped 83.2→79.8% from norm overhead AND quality degraded. RMS norm removes scale information that SwiGLU gating relies on. Over-norming: input_norm→gate*up→hidden_norm→proj→output_norm is 3 sequential norms which constrains expressiveness

resid_lambdas init 1.0→1.05 (hypothesis: stronger skip connections improve gradient flow in 16-layer model; evidence: modded-nanogpt uses 1.1^0.5≈1.048): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8845 WORSE by 0.002 at noise threshold — amplified residual didn't improve quality; model may already have optimal residual scaling from Peri-LN double-norm. Skip connection strength not the bottleneck

gated attention per-head sigmoid gate Y'=Y*σ(XW) init bias=4.0 (hypothesis: input-dependent head sparsity breaks plateau; evidence: Qwen NeurIPS 2025 best paper <2% overhead): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8912 WORSE by 0.009 — despite proper init (sigmoid(4)≈0.98 near pass-through) quality degraded. 2% MFU drop (83.2→81.9) means fewer tokens (194M vs 189M) AND gate computation adds noise to gradient flow through attention. At 6 heads per-head gating too coarse; paper validated at larger scales (1.7B+). Both MoH and gated attention fail at this scale — head gating needs more heads to be beneficial

causal depthwise conv1d kernel=3 replacing token shift identity init (hypothesis: learnable local mixing richer than fixed shift; evidence: hybrid conv-attn architectures): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8906 WORSE by 0.008 — MFU dropped 83.2→81.6% yielding 6% fewer tokens (183M vs 189M); conv adds overhead without sufficient quality gain to compensate. 3D conv weights handled by AdamW not Muon (further hurting optimization). Simple token shift is more efficient at this scale

torch.compile mode=reduce-overhead CUDA graphs (hypothesis: less Python overhead improves MFU): CRASH — CUDA graphs incompatible with flex_attention block mask caching (tensor output overwritten by subsequent run). reduce-overhead mode cannot work with dynamic mask tensors in flex_attention

housglass MLP K=2 stacked SwiGLU sub-MLPs hidden 2048→2×1024 same params (hypothesis: deeper nonlinear composition per FLOP; evidence: Feb 2026 arxiv 2602.06471 at 113-403M): val_bpb 0.8825→0.9015 WORSE by 0.019 — MFU dropped 83.2→78.9% from smaller matmuls (768×1024 less efficient than 768×2048 on RTX 5070 tensor cores); 5% fewer tokens (180M vs 189M); the sequential SwiGLU path adds latency per layer. Deeper MLP composition does NOT overcome throughput loss at this scale. Single wide MLP is more hardware-efficient

RoPE base 10000→1024 (hypothesis: concentrate rotary frequencies within 2048 context range; evidence: modded-nanogpt uses base=1024): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8906 WORSE by 0.008 — MFU dropped 83→79.5% and 4% fewer tokens (182M vs 189M). Base=1024 compresses frequencies too much for our 229M/16-layer/Peri-LN architecture; optimal base is architecture-dependent not universal

SHORT_WINDOW 256→128 (hypothesis: halve S-layer attention cost for more throughput; evidence: modded-nanogpt uses 128): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8830 noise-level 0.0006 — throughput improved (85.6 vs 83.2% MFU 192.5M vs 189M tokens) but quality per step slightly worse offsetting gain. 128 too narrow for S-layers at 229M/16-layer scale

per-sublayer learnable attn_scales/mlp_scales init=1.0 (hypothesis: learnable attn/MLP balance improves deep feature learning; evidence: modded-nanogpt per-sublayer scaling): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8836 noise-level 0.001 — throughput improved (84.8 vs 83.2% MFU 194M vs 189M tokens) but quality-per-step unchanged. Peri-LN double-norm already provides sufficient sublayer scaling; extra learnable scales are redundant

layer-scaled MLP widths by depth hidden_dims 1568→2528 around 2048 average (hypothesis: later layers need more FFN capacity at fixed parameter budget, evidence: OpenELM-style layer-wise scaling + plateau after 5 non-crash runs): crashed before first step with "input must be contiguous"; forcing contiguous activations at attention/MLP boundaries did NOT fix it. Rules out this heterogeneous per-layer MLP-width design on the current torch.compile+MXFP8+checkpointing stack

HEAD_DIM 128→192 (6 heads→4 at fixed 768 width; hypothesis: larger per-head capacity improves attention expressivity, evidence: HEAD_DIM 64 was worse despite more tokens): crashed at compile with Triton resource error "No valid triton configs" / fused rms_norm+flex_attention out of resource. Rules out 192-dim heads on this Blackwell+torch.compile stack without deeper kernel/workload changes

TRANSPONDER input-adaptive residual gates: per-token sigmoid(Linear(x)) gate on attn+MLP sublayer outputs init bias=3.0 (hypothesis: dynamic content-aware gating breaks plateau; evidence: TRANSPONDER paper 5-15% perplexity reduction at 60-250M scale): val_bpb 0.8825→0.9094 WORSE by 0.027 — MFU dropped 83.2→75.6% yielding 10% fewer tokens (171M vs 189M); gate computation adds significant overhead per layer. Quality per step also degraded — sigmoid gating disrupts the Peri-LN gradient flow pattern. Input-adaptive gating NOT beneficial at this architecture/scale combination

stochastic depth linear 0→0.1 drop prob across layers compile-friendly tensor mask (hypothesis: regularization helps in undertrained regime per arXiv 2303.01500; evidence: LayerDrop ICLR 2020): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8875 WORSE by 0.005 — random block zeroing disrupts the Peri-LN gradient flow pattern; 82.4% MFU vs 83.2% baseline slight throughput cost; more tokens (194M vs 189M) but quality per step degraded. Stochastic depth not beneficial with Peri-LN double-norm architecture

global gradient norm clipping max_norm=1.0 (hypothesis: prevent gradient spikes that waste optimizer steps; evidence: standard in GPT-2/3/Llama training): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8825 IDENTICAL within noise (0.000003) — Muon Newton-Schulz already normalizes matrix param gradients; AdamW embedding params show no spike issues. Gradient clipping is redundant with Muon optimizer

partial RoPE 50%→25% (rotary_dim head_dim//4 instead of //2; hypothesis: more content-based dims help since 0→50% gave +0.004; evidence: extrapolating direction): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8820 MARGINAL 0.0005 below 0.002 threshold — throughput improved (198M vs 189M tokens 83.7% vs 83.2% MFU) from less RoPE compute but quality per step degraded. Optimal partial RoPE is near 50% not lower. Too little positional info (32/128 dims) hurts attention quality; 50% is the sweet spot

bigram hash embedding nn.Embedding(8192,768) hash=(36313*cur)^(27191*prev)%8192 added to wte output (hypothesis: learned bigram representations improve data efficiency; evidence: modded-nanogpt Record #62 biggest single quality win -8.5%): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8820 MARGINAL 0.0005 below 0.002 threshold — 6.3M extra params (235.3M total) and similar throughput (194M vs 189M tokens) but quality per step unchanged. Bigram info already captured by token shift channel mixing. Hash table 8192 may also be too sparse for 50257-token vocab (2.5B possible bigrams)

batch size schedule half batch 2^16 first 30% then full 2^17 (hypothesis: more optimizer steps early improves convergence; evidence: modded-nanogpt Record #46): CRASH — scoping bug total_tokens_processed not available in eval section; first run showed 1838 steps (27% more than baseline) but crashed before eval. Concept viable but needs proper implementation

Muon beta2 0.95→0.98 (hypothesis: smoother gradient normalization improves convergence in ~1500 steps; evidence: Karpathy autoresearch found beta2=0.98 helped): val_bpb 0.8825→0.8784 IMPROVED by 0.0041 — higher beta2 EMA half-life 14→35 steps provides more stable update scaling throughout training; throughput slightly improved (198M vs 189M tokens 84.3 vs 83.2% MFU) suggesting better compile behavior; biggest improvement in 25+ experiments

learnable logit_shift after softcap (hypothesis: frees model capacity from learning unigram distribution; evidence: modded-nanogpt logit shift technique): val_bpb 0.8784→0.8810 WORSE by 0.0026 — 4.7% MFU drop (84.3→80.2%) from unbounded logit_shift breaking torch.compile optimization yielding 4.5% fewer tokens (189.8M vs 198.8M); VRAM spiked 9.8→11.4GB; throughput cost outweighed any quality benefit

Muon final momentum 0.95→0.975 (hypothesis: faster convergence with smoother beta2=0.98; evidence: standard optimizers use 0.9-0.99): val_bpb 0.8784→0.8860 WORSE by 0.008 — higher momentum causes overshooting during warmdown phase; loss trajectory shows higher train loss throughout (3.34 vs 3.21 at step 290; 2.61 vs 2.57 final). Momentum 0.95 is optimal ceiling with beta2=0.98

WD schedule: constant 0.1 during warmup+peak then decay to 0 during warmdown (hypothesis: maintain regularization during exploration; evidence: constant-WD-full-training was worse suggesting decay needed, but WHEN to decay matters): val_bpb 0.8784→0.8822 WORSE by 0.004 — higher WD during peak (0.1 vs 0.05-0.1 linear decay) constrains learning too much; training loss higher throughout (3.43 vs 3.21 at step 290). Linear WD decay from start is better — gradual relaxation of regularization is optimal

AdamW beta2 0.95→0.98 for embedding/lm_head params (hypothesis: smoother gradient normalization mirrors successful Muon beta2 change; evidence: Muon beta2 0.95→0.98 gave +0.0041): val_bpb 0.8784→0.8768 MARGINAL 0.0016 below 0.002 threshold — directionally correct but not reliably distinguishable from variance. AdamW second moment smoothing helps less than Muon's because embeddings have less gradient noise than matrix params

WEIGHT_DECAY 0.1→0.05 (hypothesis: lower WD helps undertrained regime 0.87 tok/param; evidence: WD 0.5 catastrophic so tried lower): val_bpb 0.8784→0.8926 WORSE by 0.014 — GPU throttled badly last 10 steps (MFU 84→5%) corrupting final loss/warmdown. But even early steps showed worse val trajectory. Lower WD lets model overfit to training data without improving generalization; regularization at 0.1 is needed even when undertrained

norm(v) added to attention QKV normalization (hypothesis: V-norm completes HybridNorm QKV stabilization; evidence: HybridNorm arxiv 2503.04598): val_bpb 0.8784→0.8863 WORSE by 0.008 — value normalization removes scale information the attention weighted sum relies on; different value tokens SHOULD have different magnitudes for expressive output. V-norm also dropped MFU 84.3→82.2% (torch.compile interaction) yielding 2% fewer tokens

learned position embeddings nn.Embedding(2048,768) added to wte output (hypothesis: complement partial RoPE 50% with absolute position info for non-RoPE dims; evidence: partial RoPE improved +0.004 showing position matters): val_bpb 0.8784→0.8852 WORSE by 0.007 — absolute position embeddings conflict with RoPE relative encoding; MFU dropped 84→80.5% (4% fewer tokens 190M vs 198M) and quality per step degraded. Learned positions redundant: RoPE already provides position AND non-RoPE dims benefit from being position-FREE for content matching

backout lambda init=0.2 at layer 8/16 (hypothesis: subtract mid-layer residual forces later layers to produce incremental features; evidence: nanochat uses this): val_bpb 0.8784→0.8818 WORSE by 0.003 — near-zero throughput cost (83.6 vs 84.3% MFU 197.5M vs 198M tokens) but quality per step slightly degraded. With Peri-LN already normalizing sublayer outputs the residual stream is well-conditioned; subtracting mid-layer info removes useful features. Backout might work better without Peri-LN

gated value embedding: gate=3*sigmoid(Linear(x[:12])→n_heads) per-head per-token (hypothesis: input-dependent gating on ve improves over static v+ve addition; evidence: nanochat uses this with 12-channel gate): val_bpb 0.8784→0.8742 IMPROVED by 0.0042 — zero-init gate gives initial scale 1.5x; model learns to modulate ve contribution per head/token. Minimal overhead (72 params/layer 82.6 vs 84.3% MFU 195M vs 198M tokens). Breaks 8-experiment plateau!

QK attention sharpening q*1.2 k*1.2 after norm (hypothesis: sharper attention focuses on relevant tokens; evidence: nanochat uses q*1.2 k*1.2): val_bpb 0.8742→0.8810 WORSE by 0.007 — 1.44x sharper attention makes model overfocus; soft attention distribution is better for 229M model. Good throughput (83.3% MFU 196M tokens) but quality per step degraded. QK-norm + partial RoPE already provides well-calibrated attention temperature

TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^17→2^18 (hypothesis: 2x larger batch = cleaner gradients despite halved steps; evidence: 2^16 was worse so tried opposite direction): val_bpb 0.8742→0.8819 WORSE by 0.008 — same total tokens (199M) but only 759 steps vs ~1488; halved optimizer updates hurts convergence. 2^17 is the sweet spot: enough steps for learning dynamics AND enough batch size for gradient quality

attention sink tokens n_sink=4 in sliding window (hypothesis: S-layers 12/16 lack global context; Streaming LLM shows first tokens are attention sinks; evidence: SSSL pattern means 75% layers see only 256 tokens): val_bpb 0.8742→0.8812 WORSE by 0.007 — MFU dropped 82.6→78.4% yielding 5% fewer tokens (185M vs 195M); flex_attention overhead from sink mask. Near-zero cost assumption was WRONG — sink tokens in block mask add significant compile/runtime overhead

multi-resolution RoPE per-head bases log-spaced 2000-150000 (hypothesis: varied base frequencies create multi-scale attention for diverse distance encoding; evidence: YaRN/multi-scale RoPE literature + SSSL S-layers limited to 256 tokens): val_bpb 0.8742→0.8764 WORSE by 0.0022 — uniform base=10000 already optimal; extreme bases (2000 and 150000) hurt: low base compresses position info too much, high base makes RoPE nearly constant (content-only). Same throughput 83% MFU 194M tokens. Per-head frequency diversity not beneficial when partial RoPE 50% already provides position/content split

NormHead: F.normalize(lm_head.weight) for cosine similarity logits (hypothesis: decouple token frequency from semantic direction; evidence: NormHead used in InternLM/Qwen): val_bpb 0.8742→0.9150 CATASTROPHICALLY WORSE by 0.041 — cosine-similarity-only logits remove the model's ability to encode token frequency in weight norms. With softcap=15 already bounding logits, NormHead over-constrains the output layer. Training loss 2.78 vs 2.65 baseline shows underfitting. The lm_head needs weight norm freedom to learn unigram/frequency priors

batch size schedule: half batch (2^16) first 30% then full (2^17) for 28% more optimizer steps (hypothesis: more exploration steps early improves convergence; evidence: modded-nanogpt Record #46): val_bpb 0.8742→0.8769 WORSE by 0.003 — 1894 total steps but only 191.5M tokens (vs 194M baseline); noisier gradients from half-batch early phase did NOT improve exploration enough to compensate; the model benefits more from clean full-batch gradients from the start. TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^17 is optimal throughout

MLP token shift: extend token shift to MLP input (hypothesis: MLP benefits from prev position post-attn features like attention does; evidence: token shift for attention improved +0.0046): val_bpb 0.8742→0.8756 WORSE by 0.0014 noise-level — MLP already gets indirect local context through attention output; explicit shift is redundant. Extra torch.roll+cat slightly hurt throughput (193.6M vs 195M tokens 82.5 vs 84.3% MFU). Token shift only helps at the attention input stage where local context isn't yet available

EMA model weights decay=0.999 for eval (hypothesis: averaging smooths training noise for better generalization; evidence: used in DeepSeek/Llama): val_bpb 0.8742→1.0026 CATASTROPHICALLY WORSE by 0.128 — decay=0.999 with only ~1476 steps means effective averaging window spans 68% of training INCLUDING poorly-trained early steps. EMA model is a diluted average that barely converges. EMA needs either (a) much higher decay (0.9999) to average only recent steps or (b) much longer training. VRAM also spiked 10.2→11.2GB from storing weight copies

late-start EMA decay=0.999 warmdown-only (hypothesis: starting EMA late avoids polluting with early undertrained weights; evidence: prior EMA exp val_bpb 1.003 from full-training averaging): val_bpb 0.8742→0.9270 STILL CATASTROPHICALLY WORSE by 0.053 — even warmdown-only EMA (last ~40% of training) heavily dilutes the final well-trained weights. With 1461 steps the warmdown covers ~584 steps; exponential averaging at 0.999 gives effective window of ~1000 steps which reaches BACK into pre-warmdown territory. EMA fundamentally incompatible with short training runs. Conclusively rules out EMA at this training scale

differential attention (ICLR 2025): split Q,K→Q1,Q2,K1,K2 (sub_head_dim=64), y=(1-λ_init)*(SDPA(Q1,K1,V)-λ*SDPA(Q2,K2,V)) (hypothesis: noise cancellation from subtracting two softmax maps improves signal quality; evidence: ICLR 2025 oral, 65% model size for equiv quality): val_bpb 0.8742→0.8979 WORSE by 0.024 — two SDPA calls per layer dropped throughput 194M→172M tokens (73% vs 82% MFU) without quality gain. The 12% fewer tokens offset any noise-cancellation benefit. At this short training budget (1312 steps), token throughput dominates — diff attention trades compute for quality, but with only 60min the compute loss hurts more than the quality gain helps. Also VRAM spiked to 11.3GB (near limit). Diff attention needs longer training to amortize its per-step quality advantage

learnable attn temperature: per-head attn_scale init=0.2 multiplied on Q after QK-norm (hypothesis: diffuse attention early prevents premature patterns; evidence: modded-nanogpt attn_scale_start=0.1): val_bpb 0.8742→0.8847 WORSE by 0.0105 — throughput preserved (195M tokens 84% MFU same as baseline) but quality per step degraded. attn_scale=0.2 means QK logits scaled to ~20% of normal range early in training which made attention too uniform for too long. The model needs sharp attention from the start at this scale to learn position-dependent features efficiently. Different from modded-nanogpt which has 10 layers and higher LR — our 16-layer Peri-LN+QK-norm already provides sufficient attention regularization

WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5→0.7 (hypothesis: longer cosine decay phase helps convergence; evidence: WARMDOWN 0.3 was -0.010 catastrophic, 0.5 was best, trend suggests longer=better): val_bpb 0.8742→0.8717 IMPROVED by 0.0025 — confirms the trend: model benefits from extended convergence phase. With 70% warmdown the LR starts decaying at 30% progress vs 50%, giving 40% more steps in warmdown. Same throughput (194M tokens 82.3% MFU) proves this is pure schedule optimization. Breaks 7-experiment plateau!

WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.7→0.8 (hypothesis: continuing 0.3→0.5→0.7 improvement trend; evidence: each step improved so far): val_bpb 0.8717→0.8733 WORSE by 0.0016 noise-level — diminishing returns hit. 80% warmdown leaves only 15% of training at peak LR which is insufficient for exploration. The model needs at least ~25% constant-LR phase (as in WARMDOWN 0.7). Optimal warmdown is 0.7 — longer helps convergence but too long starves exploration

WEIGHT_DECAY 0.1→0.15 with existing CWD (hypothesis: slightly stronger regularization helps generalization; evidence: WD 0.05 worse WD 0.5 catastrophic pre-CWD; modded-nanogpt uses 1.2): val_bpb 0.8717→0.8714 MARGINAL 0.0003 below 0.002 threshold — not reliably distinguishable from variance. WD 0.1 already optimal with CWD at this scale; increasing to 0.15 adds no benefit but doesn't hurt either. Same throughput (195M tokens 82.5% MFU). CWD makes WD changes less impactful since it's already selective
